note: Twenty-five pages, 55 measured regions: 24 page-foot WeChat stamps, one stamp fused into Table.4's region, 12 display-equation regions and 19 exhibits - 14 figure regions plus 5 tables. The figure regions print the numbers 1 to 10 and then 11 four times (p20 Japan, p21 Yemen, and the two p23 sensitivity rasters under one caption line), with no Figure.12 anywhere, so 14 figure regions carry 14 printed numbers that use only 11 distinct values. Every table region is a different rule style: Tables 1 and 5 booktabs from exactly 3 paths, Tables 2, 3 and 4 closed frames from 277, 95 and 772 paths, Table.4's count inflated by the page-foot stamp measured inside it. Captions are uniform in side - 14 figures below, 5 tables above, gaps from 1.2 to 25.6 pt - and near-empty in content: no caption states a unit, a variable or a reading, and the numbers are set 'Figure.N' with a period so none parses as a token. The 12 excluded regions are display maths on p9, p10 and p19, including one 144-path bracketed five-line assignment group on p10. Citation is thin and partly wrong: nineteen pointer lines, six exhibits never cited, two pointers naming the wrong number, and one bare pointer on a two-exhibit page counted for nothing.
rules: This paper's census closes with arithmetic that has to be done by hand: 25 pages and 55 measured regions = 24 page-foot stamps + 1 stamp FUSED into a table region + 19 exhibits + 12 display-equation regions. The 19 exhibits are 14 figure regions and 5 tables; the 12 equation regions are all 'not-an-exhibit' exclusions, so [caption.verbatim] is quoted for 19 rows and the exclusion list holds 36 entries - 24 'background' plus 12 'not-an-exhibit'.

The stamp count is 24, not 25, because on p16 the page-foot block is measured INSIDE Table.4: that region runs [71.5,604.8,592.2,838.9], touches the page bottom and carries 772 paths, about one table's worth of rules plus the stamp's 693, so p16 has no separate stamp region to exclude and [table.rule_style] on that row describes a table sharing its box with the banner. This is the first fused stamp/table in this lane; the previous papers fused a stamp only with a caption.

The 12 equation regions are concentrated on p9 (4), p10 (7) and p19 (1), and they prove the region pass is not an exhibit pass: p10's seven regions are one bracketed five-line assignment group (144 paths, one region because the bracket is one stroke) plus six separate display equations, and p19's single region is the two-line PSO update. None of the twelve prints a caption, a number, an axis or a legend, which is why none is claimed and no row carries a [caption.verbatim] for them.

Caption side is again kind-driven and uniform: all 14 figure captions print BELOW their drawing and all 5 table captions print ABOVE their grid - Figure.1 y367.24 under a region ending 356.36, Figure.2 y695.97 under 690.88, Figure.10 y705.09 under 703.90, Figure.11 (Japan) y292.84 under 290.40, against Table.1 y208.09 over 222.62, Table.2 y73.79 over 88.32, Table.3 y285.76 over 300.29, Table.4 y590.22 over 604.75 and Table.5 y370.00 over 384.41. [caption.position] is therefore 'below' on every item row and 'above' on every table row, with gaps from 1.2 pt (Figure.10, y705.09 under 703.90) to 25.6 pt for the p23 pair, whose one caption line clears the taller of its two rasters; all five table captions sit 14.4 to 14.5 pt above their grids.

The printed numbering is outside the lane's vocabulary, so [caption.numbering] reads 'none' on 18 of the 19 rows: this paper sets every figure and table number with a PERIOD and no space - 'Figure.1', 'Figure.10', 'Table.2', 'Table.5' - which matches neither 'Figure N' nor 'Figure N.'. Only Table.1 prints the colon form the vocabulary knows ('Table 1: Notations used in this paper'), so that one row carries 'Table N:' and the other eighteen carry 'none' with the printed spelling quoted verbatim in [caption.verbatim].

The number 11 is printed FOUR times over four unrelated drawings: p20 'Prediction of ecosystem service scores in Japan', p21 'Yemen's scores compare with the world average', and the p23 sensitivity pair, whose single caption line 'Figure.11 Sensitivity Analysis about the parameter e' covers two side-by-side rasters at y308.08. Figures run 1 to 10 with no gap and then 11 four times, and no Figure.12 exists anywhere, so [caption.verbatim] repeats across rows and the printed number can never identify a figure in this paper.

The two rasters under that shared p23 caption are not captioned as a pair: the (a)/(b) letters that distinguish them print three lines BELOW the drawings, inside the body sentence 'Figure.11.(a) and Figure.11.(b).', not on the caption line. The body text then resolves them by content - 11(a) 'reveals the process of PSO algorithm' and 11(b) is the parameter-e study - which makes 11(a) the RIGHT-hand raster [310.97,...] and 11(b) the left-hand one [87.00,...]. [geometry.legend] is 'inside' on 11(b) for its boxed two-entry MAPE/swarms key and 'none' on 11(a).

Every table here is either fully ruled or booktabs by a three-path signature: Tables 2, 3 and 4 measure from 277, 95 and 772 paths as closed frames with column and row rules, so [table.rule_style] is 'boxed' on those three rows, while Tables 1 and 5 each measure from exactly 3 paths - top rule, header rule, bottom rule - and are 'booktabs'. Table.4's 772 paths include the fused page-foot stamp, so that row's path count is not a pure table measure.

Two tables duplicate a header cell across two different columns: Table.3 prints 'targets' over both a percentage column and a percentage-change column, and Table.2 prints 'Weights' over two unsynchronised weight sets at two levels. [table.header_rows] is 1 on every table here - no table in this paper uses a second printed header row - and [table.merged_cells] is true only on Tables 2 and 3, which are the two with spanning cells.

Every table is text-only, so [table.numeric_cols] is 0 on Tables 1, 4 and 5 and 2 on Tables 2 and 3, and [table.decimal_aligned] is false on all five: Table.2's four-decimal weights line up by left edge and Table.3's percentages by right edge, so no column is aligned on its decimal point even where the values look columnar.

Families over the fourteen figure regions: 8 line, 2 map-or-plan-view, 2 flowchart-or-schematic, 1 node-link-network and 1 other. The 'other' row is Figure.11 on p21, a radar chart the closed vocabulary does not name, and [geometry.printed_numbers] is false there because no ring prints a value; the two maps carry printed class bounds only, and [geometry.legend] is 'outside-left' on both, 'outside-right' on the three costs/benefits curve panels, 'above' on the radar and 'inside' on the p23 parameter-e panel.

Panel count is per image, not per drawing grid: the p23 pair is TWO separate raster regions fed by one caption line, so [geometry.panel_count] is 1 on both rows and the pair is recovered from [caption.verbatim] repeating plus the body-text letters, not from a panel count. Nothing in this paper is drawn in 3D, so [geometry.three_d] is 'no' on every row.

Citations are nineteen pointer lines in twenty-five pages, eighteen of them counted onto a row, and SIX exhibits are never cited at all: Figures 1, 2 and 9, Figure.11 (Japan), Figure.11 (Yemen) and Table.2. [mention.count] is 2 on six rows - Table.3 ('following table3' plus 'From the above table'), Table.4 ('the table below' plus 'the above table4'), Figure.5 (cited on p12 and again on p17), Figure.7 (p17 and p18), Figure.11(a) and Figure.11(b) (the joint line plus each own sentence) - and 1 on seven rows, which is thirteen cited rows out of nineteen.

Two pointers are mis-pointers and are counted for the number actually printed, not for the content they describe: p17's 'Figure5 is used to show the change of benefits and costs' names Figure.5 but describes the costs/benefits curves only Figure.7 holds, and p17's 'the above table4' names Table.4 for data Table.4's four bulleted service lists do not contain. [mention.lead_pages] is signed and honest: Figure.3 is cited on p6 and printed on p7, so that row carries +1 - a pointer one page early - while Figure.4 carries -1, because its only pointer sits on p12, a page after the map on p11. [mention.style] on the Figure.5 row carries only 'Figure 5', the spelling on the cited page, because the glued spelling 'Figure5' of its second, mis-pointing citation sits on p17 - four pages past the window a style string is verified against - so that spelling is quoted in the row's note instead of the style list.

Bare pointers name no number and are counted only when their page holds exactly one exhibit: the p16 'The results are shown in the table below' is counted for Table.4 and the p19 'The predicted results are shown in the figure below' for Figure.10, [mention.style] holding the bare words 'table' and 'figure' as printed. The p18 pointer 'The following figure shows the results' sits on a page with two exhibits and is counted for neither rather than guessed onto one.

Printed defects are recorded per row: 'Methed' for Method and 'Environ ment' in Figure.1, 'emoissons', 'GDP per capital', 'sco-economic' and 'Ecosyste m' in Figure.3, ASCII '<=9.9' and an unnamed index in Figure.4, an unlabelled grey class in Figure.5, 'disturbance' set where an axis title belongs in Figure.6, 'Times' mis-set as an axis title in Figure.7, 'Faster Recovery' against 'Slower recovery' plus a stray second 'Time' in Figures 8 and 9, an endpoint of 2040 under an axis running to 2041 in Figure.10, a 75.3918 target against a 75.442 mark in Figure.11 (Japan), hyphen-broken table prose in Table.4, and the paper's watermark printing through the maps of Figures 4 and 5 and through the box of Table.5. The same reading is why [geometry.printed_numbers] is true on only six of the fourteen figure rows - the two maps and the four ticked line panels - and false on the flowcharts, the concept map, the sketch and the radar, none of which prints a single number.
